content.text:
Here are the **best laptop deals I’d check first online today (May 31, 2026)**. Prices can change fast, so treat these as “verify before checkout” picks.

## Best laptop deals by use case

| Best for | Deal to check | Why it’s a good deal |
|---|---:|---|
| **Budget Windows laptop** | **Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x — $599.99** | PCWorld’s top budget pick; listed as **$370 off**. Good everyday/student option if you want low cost without going ultra-cheap. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3145503/best-memorial-day-laptop-deals.html?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Ultra-cheap basic laptop** | **HP 14" Intel N150, 4GB/128GB — $199.99 at Best Buy** | Very low price for web, email, docs, streaming. I’d only buy this if your needs are light; 4GB RAM is limiting. ([bestbuy.com](https://www.bestbuy.com/discover/trending-deals/trending-deals-laptops-computers/pcmcat1752523872274?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Best mainstream Windows value** | **HP OmniBook X Flip 14" 2K Touch, Core Ultra 5, 16GB/512GB — $649.99 at Best Buy** | Much better long-term specs than the $199 tier: 16GB RAM, SSD, touchscreen, 2-in-1 design. ([bestbuy.com](https://www.bestbuy.com/discover/trending-deals/trending-deals-laptops-computers/pcmcat1752523872274?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Large-screen productivity** | **LG gram Max 17 — $1,299.99** | PCWorld’s top portable deal; listed as **$300 off**. Best if you want a big screen without a heavy gaming laptop. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3145503/best-memorial-day-laptop-deals.html?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MacBook deal** | **15-inch MacBook Air M5, 16GB/512GB — $1,149 at Best Buy** | Strong pick if you want macOS, long battery life, and a larger screen. 16GB RAM/512GB SSD is the config I’d target. ([bestbuy.com](https://www.bestbuy.com/discover/trending-deals/trending-deals-laptops-computers/pcmcat1752523872274?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Budget gaming** | **Alienware 16 Aurora — about $1,070–$1,100** | PCWorld listed it as the best gaming-laptop deal at **$1,069.97**, and Dell’s Father’s Day page shows an Alienware 16 Aurora with RTX 4050 at **$1,099.99**. Good entry-level 1080p/1440p gaming option. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3145503/best-memorial-day-laptop-deals.html?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Mid/high-end gaming** | **Alienware 16X Aurora, Core Ultra 9 / RTX 5060 / 32GB / 1TB — $1,849.99 at Dell** | Big listed discount: Dell shows **$900 off** estimated value. Stronger than basic RTX 4050 laptops and already has 32GB RAM. ([dell.com](https://www.dell.com/en-us/shop/deals?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Premium gaming / creator** | **Alienware 16 Area-51, RTX 5080 / 32GB / 2TB — $3,899.99 at Dell** | Expensive, but Dell lists **$1,000 off**. Only worth it if you need high-end GPU performance. ([dell.com](https://www.dell.com/en-us/shop/deals/pc-gaming-deals?utm_source=openai)) |

## My quick picks

- **Best overall value:** **HP OmniBook X Flip 14" for $649.99** — solid specs, modern CPU, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD.  
- **Best cheap laptop:** **HP 14" for $199.99** — only for very light use.  
- **Best student/work laptop:** **Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x for $599.99** or **MacBook Air M5 for $1,149** if you prefer macOS.  
- **Best gaming value:** **Alienware 16 Aurora around $1,070–$1,100**.  
- **Best power-user gaming deal:** **Alienware 16X Aurora RTX 5060 for $1,849.99**.

## What I’d avoid

- **4GB RAM Windows laptops** unless you only browse, email, and stream.  
- **8GB RAM gaming laptops** unless RAM is upgradeable.  
- “Huge discount” listings with old CPUs, tiny SSDs, or 1366×768 displays.  
- Paying extra for AI/Copilot branding unless the base specs are also good.

If you tell me your **budget**, **Mac vs. Windows preference**, and whether you need it for **school, work, gaming, or travel**, I can narrow this to the top 3 deals worth buying.
